note: 'verified': true = name and units confirmed in a real NASA POWER monthly response (API v2.10.0). 'verified': false = a documented POWER parameter that has NOT yet been checked by the team; the app reads its units from the live response and labels it 'units confirmed on fetch'. Run the check before relying on it.

variables.definition: How hot or cold the air is, measured about 2 metres above the ground, the height of a weather-station thermometer.
variables.why_it_matters: Temperature affects crops, water use, energy demand and how hot people feel.
variables.caveat: This is NASA's MERRA-2 model estimate for a grid cell about 50 km across, not a thermometer reading. The heat of a single city is too small to show up.

variables.definition: How much rain (and other precipitation) reaches the ground, in millimetres of water. POWER gives an average per day for each month; TERRASCAN turns it into monthly, seasonal and yearly totals.
variables.why_it_matters: Rain fills rivers, soil and reservoirs and decides how well crops grow, so more or less of it matters to farms and cities.
variables.caveat: A model estimate that has been corrected using observations, averaged over a grid cell about 50 km across. Rainfall changes a lot from year to year, so short periods can mislead.

variables.definition: How full of water vapour the air is, as a percentage of the most it could hold at that temperature. 100% means the air is saturated.
variables.why_it_matters: Humid air feels hotter and slows the drying of soil and crops, and it is part of how clouds and rain form.
variables.caveat: Relative humidity depends on temperature: warmer air can hold more water, so the percentage can fall even if the amount of water vapour stays the same. Model estimate for a grid cell about 50 km across.

variables.definition: The average of each day's highest air temperature, about 2 metres above the ground.
variables.why_it_matters: Daytime peaks drive heat stress for people, crops and livestock, and the demand for cooling.
variables.caveat: A model estimate for a grid cell about 50 km across, not a thermometer reading. Daily peaks in a city can be higher than this smooth estimate.

variables.definition: The average of each day's lowest air temperature, about 2 metres above the ground, usually just before sunrise.
variables.why_it_matters: Warmer nights give people and crops less time to cool down, and can reveal long-term warming.
variables.caveat: A model estimate for a grid cell about 50 km across. Local cold pockets and city heat are too small to appear.

variables.definition: How fast the wind blows, measured about 10 metres above the ground.
variables.why_it_matters: Wind moves moisture and heat around, dries soil, and decides how useful wind power can be.
variables.caveat: A smooth model estimate for a grid cell about 50 km across. Local gusts, buildings and hills are not represented.

variables.power_long_name: All Sky Surface Shortwave Downward Irradiance
variables.definition: How much of the Sun's energy lands on each square metre of ground, after clouds and haze have taken their share.
variables.why_it_matters: It powers plant growth and solar panels, and changes with cloud cover and air pollution.
variables.caveat: Estimated from satellite cloud data and a model for a grid cell about 50 km across. Treat small changes with caution.
